title: Simultaneous generically finite flatification over integral etale charts
statement: Let $X$ be an integral Noetherian scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], meaning it has a finite affine cover by Noetherian rings, whose affine coordinate rings are quasi-excellent [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Let $(e_i:E_i\to X)_{i\in I}$ be a finite family of separated etale morphisms of finite type with nonempty integral sources [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. No covering hypothesis is imposed. For each $i$ let $f_i:F_i\to E_i$ be proper and dominant with $F_i$ integral and with finite function field extension of degree $n_i=[k(F_i):k(E_i)]>0$ [def-weil-proper-morphism]; dominant means dense image and function field means the local ring at the generic point. Then there exist a normal integral Noetherian scheme $X'$, a proper morphism $p:X'\to X$ that is an isomorphism over a dense open of $X$, and, writing $E_i'=E_i\times_X X'$ [def-pc-fibre-product], integral Noetherian schemes $F_i'$ with finite locally free surjections $a_i:F_i'\to E_i'$ of constant rank $n_i$ [def-pc-finite-locally-free, def-weil-surjective-morphism], together with $E_i$-morphisms $F_i'\to F_i$. Each $E_i'$ is integral and normal, its projection $E_i'\to E_i$ induces an isomorphism of function fields, and $F_i'\to F_i$ also induces an isomorphism of function fields. All these schemes are of finite type over $X$. Normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain. The schemes $F_i'$ may be chosen as the scheme-theoretic closures of the generic fibres of $F_i$ in $F_i\times_X X'$: on an affine open this closure is cut out by the kernel of restriction to that generic fibre [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-closure].

source.place: Expose II, proof of Theorem 3.2.3, initial platification reduction, printed p. 30; simultaneous chart form of Raynaud--Gruson. Stacks flat.tex Tags 081R (lemma-flat-after-blowing-up), 05B9 (lemma-etale-flat-up-down), 0B48 (lemma-proper-flat-finite-over-dense-open); normalization uses morphisms.tex Tags 035S (lemma-nagata-normalization), 035Q (lemma-normalization-normal), 0BAJ (lemma-birational-isomorphism-over-dense-open), and more-algebra.tex Tag 07QV (lemma-quasi-excellent-nagata).

proof.text: Put $K_i=k(E_i)$ and $L_i=k(F_i)$. The generic fibre of $f_i$ is $\operatorname{Spec}L_i$. Indeed, on any nonempty affine open $\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $f_i^{-1}(\operatorname{Spec}A)$, dominance embeds $A$ in $B$ and the fraction-field lemma embeds $B$ in $L_i$. Thus $B\otimes_AK_i$ is a subalgebra of the finite-dimensional $K_i$-vector space $L_i$, is a domain, and has fraction field $L_i$. Multiplication by a nonzero element on this finite-dimensional domain is injective and hence surjective; it is therefore a field and equals $L_i$. These affine pieces all have the same generic point of $F_i$, so their generic fibres glue to that single spectrum.

source.place: Tag 01RV, lemma-integral-scheme-rational-functions; elementary finite-dimensional domain argument

proof.text: The sources $E_i$ and $F_i$ are Noetherian: the given maps are of finite type, proper maps are of finite type, and finite type is closed under composition. Properness also makes $f_i$ quasi-compact and separated, hence quasi-separated. The generic-finite neighbourhood lemma applies to $f_i$, by Step 1, and supplies an open $V_i\subseteq E_i$ containing its generic point over which $f_i$ is finite.

Form $W=\coprod_{i\in I}F_i$ and let $g:W\to X$ have components $e_if_i$. This is finite type and separated: locally on each open-and-closed component these properties hold for $e_if_i$, and the finite family supplies quasi-compactness; the diagonal has empty off-diagonal components. Generic flatness applied to $g$ gives a nonempty open $U\subseteq X$ over which $g$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. The scheme $X$ is quasi-compact by its finite affine cover and quasi-separated by local Noetherianness; $U$ is quasi-compact since $X$ is Noetherian. Thus $X,U,g$ meet all hypotheses of the flattening theorem. If $I$ is empty take $W=\varnothing$ and $U=X$.

source.place: Tag 052A, proposition-generic-flatness; Tags 01KU, 01T3; finite disjoint union argument

proof.text: Apply flattening to $g$ and $U$. Obtain a $U$-admissible blowup $b:B\to X$ for which the strict transform $T$ of $W$ is flat and of finite presentation over $B$. Let $O=X\setminus V(\mathcal I)$ for the centre ideal. It contains $U$, and $B\times_XO\simeq O$. The blowup is proper, hence finite type. Its standard affine charts over an integral affine $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset X$ have rings $A[\mathcal I/a]\subseteq A_a$. Nonempty charts are domains, and their common open over $O$ is dense in every chart: localization at the nonzero $a$ embeds the chart ring in $A_a$. Hence $B$ is integral and has function field $k(X)$. It is Noetherian and all its affine coordinate rings are quasi-excellent, by finite-type stability.

source.place: Tag 081R, lemma-flat-after-blowing-up; divisors.tex Tag 0804, lemma-blowing-up-affine; More on Algebra Tag 07QU

proof.text: Set $E_{i,B}=E_i\times_XB$. The open-and-closed decomposition $W\times_XB=\coprod_i(F_i\times_XB)$ restricts the strict transform $T$ to closed subschemes $T_i\subseteq F_i\times_XB$. This follows directly from the closure characterization: its defining ideal restricts separately on disjoint open components. Each $T_i\to B$ is flat and locally of finite presentation, and its restriction over $O$ is $F_i\times_XO$. Each $E_{i,B}\to B$ is etale. At $t\in T_i$ mapping to $z\in E_{i,B}$, the etale local-ring flatness lemma, applied to $M=\mathcal O_{T_i,t}$, changes flatness over $\mathcal O_{B,b(z)}$ into flatness over $\mathcal O_{E_{i,B},z}$. Consequently $T_i\to E_{i,B}$ is flat.

The morphism $T_i\to E_{i,B}$ is proper: it is the composite of its closed immersion in $F_i\times_{E_i}E_{i,B}$ and the base change of $f_i$. The target $E_{i,B}$ is Noetherian by finite-type base change and finite-type permanence; properness and the locally-Noetherian finite-presentation lemma therefore make $T_i\to E_{i,B}$ locally of finite presentation.

The open $D_i=E_{i,B}\times_{E_i}(V_i\cap e_i^{-1}O)$ is dense in $E_{i,B}$. To check this, the etale map $E_{i,B}\to B$ is open, so any nonempty open in $E_{i,B}$ meets the inverse image of the dense open $b^{-1}O$ of $B$. That inverse image is identified with the nonempty open $e_i^{-1}O$ of the integral scheme $E_i$. It meets $V_i$ densely. Here $e_i^{-1}O$ is nonempty because the nonempty etale source $E_i$ maps openly to the integral $X$, so its image meets $O$. Over $D_i$, the morphism $T_i\to E_{i,B}$ is the finite map $f_i|_{V_i}$ restricted further. Apply the proper-flat finiteness lemma, using Step 6 for local finite presentation, to conclude that $T_i\to E_{i,B}$ is finite, flat and locally of finite presentation.

Let $\nu:X'\to B$ be the componentwise normalization of the integral $B$. On an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq B$, it is $\operatorname{Spec}\overline A$, where $\overline A$ is the integral closure of $A$ in $k(X)$. Quasi-excellence makes $A$ Nagata. As $A$ is a domain, the zero-prime clause of the Nagata definition says it is Japanese, and the degree-one case of that definition makes $\overline A$ a finite $A$-module. The integral-closure normality lemma says $\overline A$ is a normal domain with fraction field $k(X)$. Its localizations are normal domains. The affine normalization description and localization compatibility therefore give an integral normal scheme $X'$ finite over $B$.

There is a nonempty open of $B$ on which $
u$ is an isomorphism. Indeed choose a nonempty affine $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq b^{-1}O$ and finite $A$-module generators $c_1,\ldots,c_r$ of $\overline A\subseteq\operatorname{Frac}A$. Write $c_j=a_j/d_j$ with $d_j
e0$. For $d=\prod_jd_j$ one has $\overline A_d=A_d$; localization compatibility identifies this with the restriction of $
u$. Since $b$ is an isomorphism over $O$, the nonempty $D(d)$ is also an open of $X$. Thus $p=b
u$ is an isomorphism on a dense open of $X$. It is proper since finite maps are proper and proper maps compose. It is finite type, and $X'$ is Noetherian by finite-type permanence.

source.place: Tag 0BAJ, lemma-birational-isomorphism-over-dense-open, finite birational affine denominator argument

proof.text: For $E_i'=E_i\times_XX'$, base change gives an etale map $E_i'\to X'$, and finite-type permanence makes $E_i'$ Noetherian. The normal-components lemma writes it as a finite disjoint union of open-and-closed normal integral schemes. Let $H\subseteq X$ be the dense open on which $p$ is an isomorphism. Every nonempty open of $E_i'$ meets the inverse image of $p^{-1}H$, because its image under the open map to $X'$ is nonempty open and $p^{-1}H$ is dense in the integral $X'$. This inverse image is $e_i^{-1}H$, a nonempty integral open in $E_i$. It cannot meet two disjoint open-and-closed components. Hence $E_i'$ has exactly one component and is normal integral. The identification over $H$ also identifies its function field with $K_i$.

source.place: Tags 02GO, 033C; normal components and openness; Tag 01RV

proof.text: Define $F_i'=T_i\times_{E_{i,B}}E_i'$ via the canonical map $E_i'\to E_{i,B}$ induced by $\nu$. On an affine $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq E_{i,B}$, write its finite inverse image as $\operatorname{Spec}C$. Over an affine $\operatorname{Spec}A'$ of $E_i'$ mapping there, the inverse image is $\operatorname{Spec}(C\otimes_AA')$; finite generators of $C$ tensor to finite generators. Thus $a_i:F_i'\to E_i'$ is finite. It is flat by flat base change and locally of finite presentation by base-change permanence, hence finite locally free by definition. The projections give the requested $E_i$-morphism $F_i'\to F_i$. Over the generic point of $E_i'$, it is $\operatorname{Spec}L_i\to\operatorname{Spec}K_i$, since both the blowup and normalization preserve the function fields and the strict transform agrees with $F_i$ on the dense open $O$.

source.place: Tags 01U9, 01TS; affine tensor calculation for finite base change

proof.text: The finite-locally-free pushforward lemma makes $a_{i*}\mathcal O_{F_i'}$ locally free of locally constant finite rank. On the connected integral $E_i'$ this rank is constant, and Step 11 identifies its generic value with $\dim_{K_i}L_i=n_i$. On each affine trivializing neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}A$ its algebra $C$ is free of rank $n_i$. Tensoring with any residue field gives a vector space of dimension $n_i>0$, so its finite-dimensional nonzero algebra has a maximal ideal and its spectrum is nonempty. This proves surjectivity and constant fibre rank $n_i$.

On every nonempty affine $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq E_i'$, the finite inverse image is $\operatorname{Spec}C$. Flatness and the affine criterion make $C$ a flat $A$-module. Since $A$ is a domain, the flat-torsionfree lemma shows $C\hookrightarrow C\otimes_AK_i=L_i$. Thus $C$ is a domain and its fraction field is $L_i$: its localization by $A\setminus\{0\}$ already equals that field. These affine inverse images share their generic point $\operatorname{Spec}L_i$, are reduced and are nonempty by Step 12. They cover $F_i'$, so $F_i'$ is integral with function field $L_i$. The projection to $F_i$ induces the identity on $L_i$, as may be checked on the common generic fibre of Step 11.

source.place: Tag 0539, flat implies torsion-free; Tag 01RV; affine localization argument

proof.text: Finally $F_i'$ is the scheme-theoretic closure of that generic fibre in $F_i\times_XX'$. It is already a closed subscheme there, by base change of the closed immersion defining $T_i$. For any nonempty affine open of $F_i'$, its coordinate ring embeds in $L_i$ by integrality and the fraction-field lemma. Therefore restriction to its generic point has zero kernel. On an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R$ of the ambient scheme, with $F_i'$ cut out by $J$, this says $J=\ker(R\to\Gamma(G,\mathcal O_G))$, where $G$ is the intersection of the generic fibre with this open; if the intersection with $F_i'$ is empty then both ideals are the unit ideal. This is precisely the asserted affine kernel description of closure. All schemes constructed are finite type over $X$: $p$ is proper, the $E_i'$ are finite type over $X'$ by base change, and $a_i$ is finite and hence finite type. Thus the $F_i'$ are Noetherian as well.

Steps: S1 generic fibre = Spec L_i (B⊗K_i is a finite-dimensional domain inside L_i). S2 Noetherianity, and 02NW applies (qcqs, finite generic fibre). S3 generic flatness on the finite coproduct, which meets the qcqs and quasi-compact-U hypotheses of 081R; I = ∅ is handled. S4 blowup B is O-admissible and integral (charts A[I/a] ⊆ A_a with a ≠ 0, D(a) dense over O); quasi-excellence passes to B by 07QU. S5 the strict transform splits over the components and 05BA transfers flatness to E_{i,B}. S6 closed immersion followed by base change of f_i, so proper and lfp. S7 D_i ≅ V_i ∩ e_i^{-1}O is dense (étale maps are open), so 0B48 gives finiteness. S8 the normalization is finite via Nagata/N-2; normal domains, localization. S9 Ā_d = A_d with D(d) ⊆ b^{-1}O ≅ O, so p is an isomorphism over a dense open. S10 every normal component meets the irreducible open e_i^{-1}H, so E_i′ is integral. S11 base change gives finite flat lfp; the generic fibre is L_i because H ⊆ O. S12 rank is constant n_i > 0, so a_i is surjective and of degree n_i. S13 flat ⇒ torsion-free, so C ⊆ L_i and F_i′ is integral. S14 closed by base change; J = ker(R → L_i); the empty case gives the unit ideal. Duplicate search: lem-trf-finite-after-blowup and lem-trf-finite-eta-flatification are weaker (single base, no normal birational X′).
